headline.purpose: The sheet heading in Akira Expanded Outline; one per page. 2rem below 60rem.

display.purpose: The series name on the sleeve, uppercase, balanced wrap. 1.75rem below 60rem.

dock-number.purpose: The STV number in the dock card, in Signal Orange. 1rem below 60rem.

closing.purpose: The end-of-sheet statement (You're all caught up). 1.25rem below 60rem.

range.purpose: The STV range on the sleeve, under a 2px ink rule.

catalogue.purpose: The STV number as the first column of each row. 0.875rem below 60rem.

title.purpose: Item titles in rows and the dock; underlined on hover only.

body.purpose: Page default; notes and series meta.

nav.purpose: Group tabs in the top bar.

label.purpose: Control text. Load more runs at 0.875rem.

meta.purpose: Source names and dates, in Muted Grey on paper or On-Ink Muted on ink.

narrative.overview:
Starve is set as a record label's release sheet. The timeline is the label's current releases: each item carries a catalogue number (STV plus its four-digit id), rows are ruled off like a printed sheet, and the series being browsed sits on an orange sleeve beside it. It is a document you work through to the end, not a feed of cards. What is playing is pulled out of the sheet and filed in the sleeve as a black sleeve card, so the release you are listening to stays in view while the sheet scrolls and swaps.

The world is three inks on paper. Black ink carries text, rules, the top bar and anything live; the off-white paper is the sheet; one signal orange marks the series sleeve and whatever is current or playing. One extended, heavy face, Akira Expanded, sets every word on the page; its outline cut sets the sheet heading. Corners are square everywhere. Structure comes from ink rules at two weights, not from boxes, shadows or tints.

Density is a working sheet: one row per item with generous vertical padding, catalogue number first, so the eye scans numbers and titles in a column. State is shown by inversion, not decoration: the playing row turns black with an orange number and its Play control reads "Playing". Motion is 150ms colour changes plus one 320ms widening of the sleeve when a player docks; all of it disappears under reduced motion.
keyCharacteristics: Black, off-white and one signal orange; no other hues, no gradients, no tints.
Akira Expanded for all text, Akira Expanded Outline for the sheet heading; Archivo at 125% width is the shipped fallback.
1px ink rules between rows, 2px ink rules for structure.
Outlined rectangular controls that invert on hover; one filled control per region.
Live state shown by inverting a whole row to ink and docking a black sleeve card in the orange column.

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Orange means "the series you are in" or "live now". It appears on the sleeve and on current or playing state only; a static row, heading or control at rest on the sheet never turns orange.

rules.name: The Inversion Rule
rules.body: State is shown by swapping ink and paper, not by tinting. Hovered controls fill with ink (with on-ink on ink grounds); the playing row becomes an ink row with on-ink text. There are no grey hover washes or translucent overlays.

rules.name: The One Face Rule
rules.body: Every word on every surface is set in Akira Expanded; the only other cut is Akira Expanded Outline, and it belongs to the page heading alone. Do not introduce a second family for reading text or controls.

rules.name: The Licensed Fallback Rule
rules.body: Akira Expanded and its outline cut are user-supplied personal-use fonts (Typologic). They are self-hosted from `/fonts/` but gitignored and never committed, because the repository is public. Archivo (committed, OFL) is the declared fallback, set at 125% width with weights 900 / 600 / 400 so a fresh clone or Docker image renders a wide Archivo with a working hierarchy. Every font stack ends in Archivo; nothing loads from a CDN.

rules.name: The Catalogue Number Rule
rules.body: Every item is identified by "STV " plus its id zero-padded to four digits, set in the Catalogue style as the first column of its row and in the Dock Number style in the dock. Ranges use an en dash ("STV 0106–0155").

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: Nothing floats. If a region needs to stand apart, give it an ink or orange ground or a 2px rule, never a shadow or a raised card.

rules.name: The Rule Weight Rule
rules.body: 1px separates like from like; 2px closes or opens a structure. Do not introduce a third rule weight for separation.

rules.name: The One Filled Control Rule
rules.body: Each region has at most one filled control: Mark all read in the bar, Playing in the playing row. Every other control is outlined and fills only on hover.

rules.name: The Docked Player Rule
rules.body: Playback lives in the sleeve, not in the sheet. Navigation, filters and bulk actions swap only the sheet, bar and series block, so the dock and its embed are never re-rendered while something plays.

dos: Do reuse the ink top bar (with its group tabs and filled bar control), the outline-cut sheet heading, the orange sleeve column, the ruled row grid with the catalogue number first, the outlined controls and the 2px end-of-sheet rule on every new surface; the Sources page should be a sheet of ruled source rows beside the same sleeve, so the whole app reads as one catalogue.
Do keep orange to the sleeve and to current or live state (current tab underline, playing row, dock number, focus on ink, selection).

Do show state by inverting ink and paper, with 150ms colour transitions (`cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)`); the sleeve's 320ms widening is the only longer motion, and none of it runs under reduced motion.
Do separate rows with 1px ink rules and mark structure with 2px ink rules.
Do set every word in Akira Expanded, the page heading in Akira Expanded Outline, and end every font stack in the self-hosted Archivo at 125% width.
Do keep the Akira files out of git; the public repository ships only Archivo and its OFL licence.
Do keep figures tabular and catalogue numbers zero-padded to four digits.
donts: Don't round corners, add shadows, or lift anything onto a card.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, gradients, or tinted surfaces.
Don't put more than one filled control in a region.

Don't add `text-transform` to content (titles, sources, notes, control labels); only the label's own marks (wordmark, series name, sheet heading, closing statement) are uppercased in CSS, so the Archivo fallback still reads content in its own case.
Don't replace control words with icons.
Don't add engagement chrome (avatars, counts of likes or views, recommendation rails); the sheet lists only what the owner subscribed to.
